features.name: NexusEventBus typed pub/sub
features.description: In-process typed event bus: subscribe(EventType, Callable), emit(EventEnvelope). Persists events per-session to JSONL. Relays USER_SIGNAL events to JSONL bridge file.

features.name: EventEnvelope with correlation_id threading
features.description: Pydantic typed event envelope: event_id (UUID), type (enum), timestamp, source, target, correlation_id, session_id, payload. correlation_id chains request→response across async hops, enabling audit trail per tool call.
features.counter_case: Cortex's sync MCP call model has no inherent async chains to correlate — the overhead may exceed the benefit until multi-agent (Phase 43) lands.

features.name: Session-scoped JSONL event sourcing
features.description: Each session writes events_<session_id>.jsonl to persistence dir. Complete typed event history survives restarts; enables log replay and audit.
features.counter_case: Cortex already has experience.jsonl and log.jsonl — adding session-scoped files adds more fragmentation to the already balkanized storage (flaw #55).

features.name: usage-report.py real Claude Code cost analytics
features.description: Reads ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl (actual Claude Code session logs). Breaks down by model/project/day. Computes real cache hit %, API cost estimates, heuristic callouts. --json for machine output.
features.counter_case: The JSONL schema in ~/.claude/projects/ is undocumented and could change across Claude Code versions, making this script fragile to upstream changes.

features.name: ConnectionManager safe broadcast + stale pruning
features.description: WebSocket pool: connect, disconnect, broadcast(). Iterates copy of connections list in broadcast; removes stale connections on send failure. Prevents RuntimeError on mutation during iteration.
features.counter_case: Phase 8.1 is a TypeScript server; the Python pattern translates but the list-copy trick is language-specific and may not be needed in Node.js event-loop semantics.

features.name: Permissive event enrichment on partial agent events
features.description: Fills missing fields (event_id, type, source, target, session_id, timestamp) on partial events written by the agent before injecting into bus. Prevents Pydantic validation failures from incomplete agent output.
features.counter_case: Permissive enrichment hides schema drift — if an agent starts omitting a field the server silently fills it, masking a bug. Cortex's strict Pydantic approach is actually safer.

features.name: Ghost Bridge dual-WebSocket fast lane
features.description: Dedicated /ws/ghost WebSocket for streaming IDE snapshots, separate from /ws/nexus event socket. Low-latency path bypasses event bus overhead for high-frequency streaming.
features.counter_case: Two WebSocket endpoints adds operational complexity; Cortex's single Phase 8.1 endpoint with message-type routing is simpler for the graph-stream use case.

features.name: text.chunk / text.final streaming event types
features.description: Dedicated enum values for streaming token output: TEXT_CHUNK for incremental tokens, TEXT_FINAL for complete response. Enables client-side progressive rendering of LLM output.
features.counter_case: Cortex's Phase 8.1 streams graph state changes, not LLM token output — the text.chunk pattern is only relevant if Cortex adds a live synthesis output stream, which isn't planned.

features.name: Agent persona loading from BOOTSTRAP.md markers
features.description: Reads BOOTSTRAP.md for ACTIVATE @<agent-name> marker, extracts following persona line. No server restart needed — live file re-read per request. Fallback to default persona.
features.counter_case: Phase 4.8 plans MCP-level persona prompts which are more structured; file markers are a quick-and-dirty approach that doesn't scale to many agents.

features.name: JSONL file-based agent bridge (inbound/outbound)
features.description: inbound.jsonl / outbound.jsonl for IDE↔backend agent communication. File bridge is local-first, no network, works cross-process.
features.counter_case: Cortex's MCP protocol is a superior message transport — typed, bidirectional, streaming-capable, and already wired into Claude Code. File bridge is a workaround for IDE integration before a proper protocol exists.

features.name: Multi-model dispatch (Gemini + OpenAI routing)
features.description: Routes LLM calls to Gemini or OpenAI based on model string prefix. Graceful error on unknown provider.

features.name: Runtime model switching via command
features.description: use model <name> text command dynamically re-routes an agent to a different LLM at runtime and persists choice to per-agent JSON config.

features.name: TaskNode with depends_on DAG chain
features.description: Pydantic schema: task_id, type, description, assigned_agent, status (WAITING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/BLOCKED), depends_on: List[str], metadata.

features.name: CORS wildcard allow_origins=["*"]
features.description: All origins allowed. Development convenience that becomes a security risk if Cortex's API ever processes sensitive code context.
features.counter_case: nexus-os is a local-only dev tool so the risk is low for them; Cortex's Phase 22 central server would be the deployment where this matters.

features.name: nexus-launcher.js concurrent process launcher
features.description: Spawns backend + frontend + ghost bridge concurrently with color-coded tagged stdout/stderr. Suppresses DeprecationWarning lines from stderr.
features.principle_violated: Local-first: Cortex is a single-process daemon; multi-process orchestration violates the single-binary principle
